-The current End Use Certificate assessment timeframe is roughly 30-60 days but could move in either direction. Payment is due within five (5) business days after the End Use Certificate receives approval.  

Please be advised of a recent requirement regarding the End Use Certificate process: the winning bidder MUST provide proof of aircraft storage upon submitting the End Use Certificate. Please be prepared to provide a valid deed or lease agreement.

- Upon approval of the End Use by DLA DoD Trade Security, the winning bidder pays GSA the purchase price. Separately: Since this aircraft is located in AMARG, a government contractor, additional fees will be assessed by AMARG. It is solely the responsibility of the winning bidder to coordinate and pay additional fees directly to AMARG (Davis-Monthan Air Force Base) to successfully remove this aircraft.


AMARG Services for prep/tow

a. Remove preservation material sufficient to access the cockpit

b. Paint over rondel and Navy markings except BUNO. Include removal of preservation as necessary to access Navy markings that may be obscured

c. Perform towability check. Change and service tire and wheel assemblies, tires/tubes to be provided by the customer

d. Pull items from the removed item (CO3) list and place in cockpit (clocks, emergency transmitter)

e. Pull and waterproof aircraft records and place in the cockpit

f. Conduct standard withdrawal items such as radiation checks

g. Prepare and tow aircraft to the MRO base side gate for transfer

Interested parties are strongly encouraged to inspect the aircraft prior to bidding or procurement. Specific engine and maintenance due questions for this aircraft are upon request.

This aircraft may NOT be in compliance with applicable FAA requirements and has neither been registered with the FAA nor maintained in accordance with FAA standards. The buyer is responsible for bringing this aircraft into compliance with applicable standards by obtaining all necessary FAA inspections or modifications.

This aircraft was certified by the United States Navy (USN) and flown under Military Type Certification (MTC) for purposes of airworthiness. It is the assuming owner's responsibility to obtain airworthiness certification from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) or equivalent agency. The USN does not possess all the technical data required to obtain such certification and it is thereby incumbent upon the owner to work with the appropriate Type Certificate (TC) and Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) holders to certify and confirm the aircraft is in the configuration desired by the operator. (1) 1944 Deck Cargo/Utility Barge, Hull ID: FB-669 is an ex-US Army BC type deck cargo/utility barge previously utilized for dry storage of ship anchors, anchor chain, and other equipment and materials in support of operations at the Suisun Bay Reserve Fleet (SBRF) in Benicia, California.  Make/Model: Unknown.  No PCBs, No Asbestos and Yes Lead Based Paint.  The interior coatings are lead-based.  The barge dimensions are 110 feet in length, 30 feet in width and a 9-foot depth.  The empty weight is approximately 120 to 150 short tons.  The condition of the barge is poor.  It was last drydocked in 2005, having the exterior sandblasted and coated with epoxy paint.  Freeboard coating is in poor condition with much corrosion visible.  The main deck exhibits extensive surface corrosion, with a few holes in the deck.  There is very little coating left on deck. It has minor, repairable damage and significant corrosion inside and out that may require maintenance or repairs. The internal compartments are coated with lead-based paint that is in poor condition.  There is approximately 4 inches of water in one of the eight compartments, presumed to be rainwater due to the holes on deck.  

The barge is offered in its current condition (operational and usable), without warranty or guarantee, expressed or implied. Prospective bidders are encouraged to conduct an on-site inspection and evaluate the condition of the barge and all included items prior to submitting a bid. The purchaser is responsible for all costs and arrangements associated with inspection, removal, towing, transportation, permits, environmental compliance, and the safe removal of the barge from the Suisun Bay Reserve Fleet.  The barge is navigational, but is not self-propelled but can be towed.  If the barge is to be towed outside of the San Francisco Bay and Delta area the hull will have to be cleaned before arrival at its destination. CA has law about transporting from one body of water to another. Bidder will need to research into this. Note: The California Marine Invasive Species Program prohibits a vessel from moving from one California port to another outside its immediate geographical area without the hull first being cleaned of biofouling (biofouling is an organism or a community of organisms that are attached to or associated with a vessels hard surfaces that are wet or underwater). For more information, please contact the California State Lands Commission.  No builders certificate or original title available. Has not been registered and not inspected by the coast guard. Used. Repairs are required.
